reply_text:
㊥ Gist: zai-2, who built the current Minard page, is now building the family figure. It will have one panel per stage colour band, each drawn in the main figure's style and opened up into that stage's top families, in shades of the band's own colour. I'm parked on the job, and when it reports back I'll check the panels against the main figure and send you the link.

㊯ (job and park) Job `invoke-1790892198239-29892-7955b4be`, park `park-a9d5866a-…`, with a 45-minute deadline.

🈖 (the design)
- **Panels:** eight, in the main figure's stage order.
- **Families:** up to eight per panel plus "other families" in grey.
- **Scale:** the same hits-per-day axis in every panel, so you can compare their thickness.
- **21 September marker:** labels before it come from the original 689 readings; after it, the 97 new provisional readings come into play as well.
- **Detail:** hovering shows family, day and hits. Below the panels, a table per stage gives each family's share before and after 21 September, with its top three patterns.
- **Tables in the write-up:** the same per-family tables go into `PATTERN-STAGES-2026-10-01.md`. The script generates them, so the numbers aren't typed in by hand.
- **Main figures:** left unchanged.

㊬ (what will make it trustworthy) One test checks that, for every stage and day, the families add up exactly to the main figure's band. It checks against the numbers embedded in the main page, not against the new script's own totals, so a counting slip in the new script can't pass unnoticed.

previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Yes, your guess holds. Comparing hits before and after 21 September, assurance rose from 23.9% to 26.5%, and most of the rise comes from three families: `test-registry`, which went from 0.7% to 3.6% of all hits, then `translation` and `contracts`. Coordination fell from 13.6% to 10.7%, mostly because `orchestration` was retrieved half as often. The shift still holds when the 97 new labels are left out, with assurance at 26.2%, so it doesn't depend on the Kimi readings.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how far this goes)
- **Topic, not act:** these are retrieval counts. They show what your turns were about, as the search engine matched them, not what each turn did. The PBASE comparison found the two hardly agree.
- **Short window:** the post-21 September window has 1,180 hits over ten days. Families with fewer than about 20 hits there could easily move by chance.
- **Family mixes span both windows:** the stage-mix column pools all hits, so a family's mix can't show a change inside that family.
